Triage: lands in `examples/app-showcase/test/vitest-console-teardown-race.test.ts`; `domain:devx` (test-infrastructure guard; examples route to the subsystem they exercise). → `pm:queue`, Bug — a 1-in-6 red on full-repo runs is merge-queue flake tax, and the card's own assertion message forbids the cheap fix (do NOT relax the GUARDED leg). Fix shape is the dev's to measure: make the ABLATION leg robust under load (attempts budget, serialized execution, or an isolated lane) while keeping its instrument value — the guard must still detect the race it exists for. Size/model suggestion: S–M, opus (the judgment sits in not weakening the guard).

- Branch: `claude/issue-11939-ablation-leg-load-robustness`

⭐ **Second finding out of the QA wave's R0 baseline** (#9298), after #11938. Both were filed as findings with nothing fixed, because R0 lands no code — and both are worth more than the round that produced them.

## The card already identifies the real gap, and it is not "a flaky test"

> If vitest ever *genuinely* fixes its console forwarding, this leg reds permanently and **looks identical to today's load flake**. The two are indistinguishable from the assertion alone.

That is the defect to close. "The instrument did not fire this time" and "the instrument is permanently dead" are different facts with different responses, and today they produce the same red with the same message. Raising the attempt budget alone would make the symptom rarer **without** separating them — so it is a partial fix at best, and the card says so.

## ⛔ The cheap fix is forbidden by the guard's own words

The assertion message ends: *"Do NOT relax the guarded leg on the strength of this."* Triage restates it. The ABLATION leg exists to prove the GUARDED leg still means something; weakening either to stop the noise destroys the reason the file exists.

## Run 6 is the control that makes this dispatchable

The card ran the file alone under **8 synthetic CPU burners on 4 CPUs (load ~7)** and it stayed **green**. So plain CPU starvation is *not* the trigger — something more specific to the full-repo condition is (many concurrent node processes, memory/scheduling pressure changing the child vitest's rpc teardown timing). Without that control the obvious fix would have been "make it tolerate load", aimed at the wrong mechanism.

⚠️ Note the sibling: **#11958** (filed from #11938) measures that vitest's own worker pool scales with host cores, uncapped, in 40/41 packages. That is plausibly the same pressure this leg is sensitive to. Read it before designing — but ⛔ do not fold it in; it has its own card and its own measurement.

Tier: **opus** — triage suggested S–M/opus and I agree. Derived live, no path-derived mandate, so sonnet is the floor and this is a judgment call: *"the judgment sits in not weakening the guard"*, and every obvious fix here trades instrument value for quiet.
